title: Independently audit all mixed-caller error budgets (no κ)
body:
Independently reproduce Ali Romman's PR6473 quantitative error contract for the exact 570-instruction mixed caller. The source establishes nine sufficient uniform guard bits and an eight-bit obstruction in its error contract; this contribution supplies separate exact implementations, retained evidence and a necessary scope clarification. The literal four-operation normalizer requires a compatible translation pair (Q² is the pair swap). For arbitrary Q^4=I, propagation instead assumes the completed-normalizer error bound 9e_s/2 explicitly; Q^4=I alone does not construct that four-operation implementation. H=C,Q=i is a simple incompatible equal-half case. The scalar 307 witness embeds in the constant sector of a four-cycle when pair compatibility is required. No numerical receipt changes. PR6433's endpoint result remains predecessor coverage.

The two engines agree on all 571 × 34 prefix rows, all 571 × 34 suffix rows, all 136 class/output coefficients and both complete 660,076-cell envelope hashes. They separately verify every normalizer error column for both signs and the literal 307 lower witness, including its complete final state. The reproduced maxima are scalar 795/2, LOCAL 28, QUERY 18, idle 28 and common 943/2. Thus 256<307<=worst amplification<=943/2<512 in the stated abstract field-error contract. No new guard theorem or optimal real amplification constant is claimed.

One engine uses four character specializations with elementary row/column operations; the other retains a formal central C4 variable and multiplies operator blocks before evaluating characters. All 18 stage symbols remain independent. Neither imports or executes author Python or its peer. Five predecessor objects are byte-authenticated before parsing. The second implementation was sealed and executed before reading the first receipt. This is separate AI implementation corroboration, not independent human or formal-kernel acceptance.

Verification: direct normal/optimized emission and strict retained receipts pass, with byte-identical emissions within each engine; five computed primary controls, separate oracle C4/source controls, eight external optimized corruption rejections, registered replay, committed bytes/modes and declared canonical provenance history pass. The official 17-file export passes integrity and read-only Git-free/empty-PATH normal/optimized replay, with unchanged bytes and modes. The published tree is exactly the tested/exported tree ab8416bf3836f3d336463e4525eb63bca0174ca3 at head 62bbf6da28ee686698d979ad9f0945f707726c9a. Both hosted jobs passed at this exact head in [run41561836466](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41561836466): all711 onboarding tests and the registered package replay. Completed logs were read once; run metadata confirms the matching head. The synthetic test commit has the same tree as the published/exported result; no actual merge was performed.

Reproduce with CPython 3.12: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/mixed-caller-error-audit`.

Scope: field 2-norm, commuting unitary stages, Q^4=I and declared completed-operation defects. Allowed lower-witness errors need not be realizable by actual rounding. No coordinate count, actual native error realization, native interior range, tape/access price, owned cleanup, physical supplier or complete compiler/outer admission is supplied. This older mixed caller is not selected PR6030. All five framework assumptions remain; no new kappa or frontier change. Selected supplier replay, Lean and Docker were not run.

Base/submission refresh: canonical main 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, priority 8, selected PR6030; all eight guidance pins unchanged. [Advance claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19363999). Bounded cached/live PR and current Discussion checks distinguish endpoint6433, LOCAL6500, scalar6499/6506 and precision6477/6478; hidden/unpublished work and arbitrary historical diffs remain unknown. Maintainer edits and auto-merge disabled; no merge requested.

ToikY with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0. Credit Ali Romman/6473 for the theorem/proof/original checker,6398/6453 mixed caller and6348 binary caller; Cinna Davis and retained native/compiler lineage; ToikY/6433 endpoint audit. Classical spectral decomposition, polynomial majorants and linear error propagation retain their credit. Exact pins, limits and original notices are retained in the package.

Task `independent-moment`, scope key `132115f71be587e238e1`: scope changed from paid-moment checking to the explicit independent-review obligation in PR6473 PROOF. This closes an independently auditable precision-contract check before any native implementation, without claiming the card's physical acceptance gate. [Open next questions](https://github.com/ToikY/integer-mult-bounds/blob/62bbf6da28ee686698d979ad9f0945f707726c9a/research/mixed-caller-error-audit/README.md#open-next-questions): bind one actual native backend and its coordinate count/rounding to the four tolerances, then prove and price native range, access and owned cleanup. That backend is currently missing. Pre-publication refresh also inspected PR6507 pricing arithmetic,6508 emitted boundary and6509 conservative rounding; none independently audits this exact error contract.

The partial-normalizer internal bound 36M+16982e is also limited to the pair-compatible four-operation realization; the all-Q grouped completed-defect premise supplies no arbitrary-Q internal range guarantee. All scientific source/code/receipt bytes remain unchanged through the scope-only follow-up commits.
